summary: Pure-Byte's 1987 Commodore 64 demo, coded by Yip with graphics by Conan: a drawn scroll-reading machine with track and scroll counters, selectable texts such as story, scores and greets, and several tunes to switch between.
why: An early C64 music-and-scroller demo built around an interactive control panel. The one CSDb comment remembers loving it as a kid and singles out the tune "5th Dream About Happiness".

quote.text: Did love this demo as kid and the tune "5th Dream About Happiness" is so fucking brilliant

summary: A 1997 ZX Spectrum 128K demo by E-Mage, built from crude hand-drawn pictures and flagged NSFW in its video title. It uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode.
why: A cheeky late-90s Spectrum oddity that Pouët voters rate well, and an example of a 128K demo using multicolour graphics.

summary: Viznut's one-man C64 demo for Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2006: a political piece with blocky abstract visuals, text slogans and a sung speech-synth soundtrack.
why: Sceners single out the singing speech synthesis, with one predicting it would start a trend in voice-synth C64 tunes. Its rough, deliberately messy look and sound divided opinion, but some call it a demo for refined taste.

quote.text: I think the voice synth tune will start a new trend in c64 tunes - gimme more voice synth!

summary: Still Rising is a two-disk-side C64 demo by Artline, Bloodsuckers, Extend and Orange, coded by Kakka, XMunkki and Space Man with graphics by LeroyB and music by Zardax. It came 2nd in the demo compo at Zoo 2022.
why: Sceners single out the light-sourced veiled statue, which changes viewpoint and zoom, along with Zardax's soundtrack and its nods to the golden years. Several thought it had real flow, and some preferred it to the winner.

quote.text: That light sourced veiled statue effect is incredible. The way it changes viewpoint and zoom makes it work extremely well.

summary: Iris's Oric demo, coded and drawn by Xeron with music by H0ffman, which came second in the Old School Demo compo at Nova 2024.
why: A recent Oric demo that placed second at Nova 2024. Its title plays on the His Master's Voice logo, which it redraws with raster colour running through it.
highlights: His Master's Voice dog and gramophone

summary: Dekadence's C64 demo Shareware, coded by BriteLite with graphics by H7 and music by Player One, placed third in the C64 demo compo at Zoo 2015.
why: A podium finish at Zoo 2015, and a chance to see H7's chunky, character-style graphics carry a whole Dekadence production.
highlights: radial tunnel in a framed window

summary: Inversion's debut C64 demo, coded by Blackis and zoi with graphics by Havocplague and music by Castor, which placed third in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010. It includes the fullscreen picture Heidi.
why: Sceners were surprised it was a first demo, and several said its look and Castor's score felt closer to Atari or Spectrum demos than typical C64 fare. They also praised how well the music fits the effects.

quote.text: I like the way music is attuned with demo effects.

summary: deMarche's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2010: oneframe fullscreen chunky effects in a gigascreen palette, with AY music and Covox digital drums.
why: A deliberate rip-and-convert entry for a compo that welcomed ripped code and graphics. It reworks the effect idea from the Amstrad CPC demo "DTC" and 505's music from the Atari STE demo "More or Less Zero". Source is available.

summary: Hoaxers and Wrath Designs' C64 demo that needs a 512K REU, winner of the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2013. Code by Firehawk, graphics by Joe and Grasstust, music by Response.
why: Sceners argued over the REU requirement, but even the doubters praised the visuals and flow. Joe's artwork, the swirling 'floffy' scroller, Response's Star Trek: Voyager tune and the closing globe screen are what people single out.
highlights: end screen with globe in hand

quote.text: Beautiful and unique demo. The graphics are epic! The Voyager theme is cool to listen to along with the complete soundtrack.

summary: A 128-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, which placed 5th in the 128 Byte Intro compo at Outline 2012.
why: A chance to see how much a 128-byte Atari intro can put on screen: a fifth-place entry from Outline's 128-byte compo.

summary: Fossil's C64 demo for X 2016, coded by Knut M. Clausen with design and music by Jammer, which placed 6th in the demo compo.
why: Sceners praise its fast pace and lack of filler, with smooth vectors, a face twister and Jammer's soundtrack singled out. Several rated it among their favourites of the compo despite the placing.

quote.text: I really love this one. Very polished, not a boring second. No fat on this one whatsoever.

summary: A megademo for the Commodore 16/Plus 4 by Assassins, released in November 2006, with code by Skoro and graphics from Harry, Luca, RRR and Kichy.
why: A multi-part Plus/4 megademo, uploaded by its coder. It was released outside any compo and is well liked on Pouët, with no down votes.

summary: Resource and FIRE's first Plus/4 production under the Resource label, coded by Bubis with a soundtrack by Luca. It won the Wild compo at Forever 2003 and needs a SID card.
why: A Wild compo winner at Forever 2003 and Resource's debut on the Plus/4, a machine many of the group originally came from. Luca's soundtrack was composed exclusively for it.

summary: Taquart's 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit, coded by Eru with music by X-Ray, which won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2008.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2008 that fits code and music into 1K.
highlights: twisting shapes over a character grid

summary: Genesis Project's two-disk-side C64 demo, coded by Raistlin, Elder0010 and Sparta, which placed 4th in the demo compo at X 2023. It is a trackmo packed with graphics, raster and sideborder effects, dedicated to Shadow.
why: Sceners praise its polish, smooth transitions and old-school code tricks: sideborder Kefrens bars with 206 bars, a perspective chessboard, a spiral scroller and a smooth double scroller. It was nominated at Siggraph Asia 2023 and the Meteoriks 2024.

quote.text: a cool modern style with smooth transitiosn with really good effects and new records to raise the bar

summary: Brainwave's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, which came second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2000.
why: A podium finish at Chaos Constructions 2000, and tagged as using the Spectrum's multicolour mode, which squeezes more colours into each character cell than the stock attribute grid allows.

summary: Desire's VBXE-enhanced Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Heaven with graphics by Ozan and SimOne and music by Triace and Vedder. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2017.
why: A podium finish at Nordlicht 2017 and a showcase for the VBXE video upgrade, which gives the Atari 800 a far richer palette than the stock machine.

summary: Censor Design's C64 demo that won the demo competition at Gubbdata 2013, with code from a team including Magnar, Bob, CRT and Mirage, graphics by Yazoo and Magnar, and Krill's loader.
why: Sceners single out the smooth square plasma, the swirl and double scrollers, the fade effects in the intro and Magnar's catchy soundtrack, along with graphics that no longer look like conversions.

quote.text: The square plasma thingy rocks! Very smooth and fresh.

summary: Artline Designs' Commodore 64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2024: a story-driven run of hires scenes following a boy through the night, with music by Flex and Mutetus.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2025. Sceners single out the atmosphere, the soundtrack, the hires graphics and the boy running through the rasters, along with the zoom scroller at the end and the side-border tricks.

quote.text: Graphics, story and the soundtrack go wonderfully hand in hand.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128 demo by Darklite and Offence, with code by Neon, music by Response and graphics by Pal. It came second in the Combined Demo compo at Black Valley 2022.
why: It placed second in a combined-platform demo compo at Black Valley 2022, and its tag marks it as a demo built around cubes.

summary: An 8K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Osmium Path, with code by Optimus and graphics and music by Ham. It came second in the intro competition at Decrunch 2022.
why: A runner-up at Decrunch 2022 that packs code, graphics and music into 8K. It's a compact example of current CPC size-limited work from Osmium Path.

summary: Resistance's ZX Spectrum 48K demo, made with RK/LE Team, which won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at speccy.pl party 2018.1. Code by Sachy, music by Dya, graphics by Fra, Slayer and At0m.
why: It took first place in the Spectrum demo compo at speccy.pl 2018.1, and three graphicians share the credits, so the hand-drawn screens carry much of the show.

summary: Life On Mars' ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2015, with code and design by introspec and music by nq.
why: A compo winner at 3BM OpenAir 2015, and the video is the final version captured at 50Hz by introspec himself.
highlights: chunky typography with long drop shadows

summary: Crest's third Krestage demo for the Commodore 64, released in 2007, with code and graphics by Crossbow and music by Jeff. It is a single-screen trick demo that pairs moving FLI pictures with VIC-chip effects in the borders.
why: Sceners were stunned by Crossbow's VIC trickery: nine sprites shown in a row, an FLI picture mover and a puzzling upper-border effect, which set off long threads working out how it was done. The bass-heavy tune gets praise too.

quote.text: Crossbow does what he does best, invent new weird things. My deepest respect!!

summary: Atlantis's C64 demo for BCC Party 2018, where it placed 4th in the demo compo. Code by Dr. Science, Merlin, q0w and Tsurugi, music by Rock and Snabel, graphics by Merlin, q0w and FatFrost.
why: Many sceners rated it above its compo placing. They single out the tunnel part, the soundtrack, the fresh credits screen, the bees linking the parts and how well it uses the party motto and Berlin.

quote.text: Lots of detail, love and creativity in here!

summary: A C64 demo by Warriors of the Wasteland, with code and music by A Life in Hell, that placed 3rd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Syntax 2008. Expect interlaced chunky modes, plasmas, 3D dots and photo-like pictures.
why: Rough and unpolished by its makers' own admission, but sceners praise its innovative code. They single out the near-photorealistic girl in the flip-disk picture and the double-colour plasma at the end.

quote.text: The girl on the flip disk part is the closest to photorealism i've ever seen on a c64.

summary: Dekadence's VIC-20 demo, coded by BriteLite with music by Roz, which placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2007.
why: A VIC-20 demo that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Assembly, a rare outing for the machine at a big party.

summary: Genesis Project cracktro for the C64 by Mermaid, who did code, graphics and music, and winner of the Intro Creation Competition 2016. A green wireframe GP logo hangs above a scrolling vector grid while a scroller runs across the middle.
why: Sceners praise its fresh, un-C64-ish Vectrex and Battle Zone style, the design of the logo and the atmospheric music. Several call it one of the best C64 intros they have seen.

quote.text: Wow! So stylish and arcade retro but still feels so fresh :) Excellent intro.

summary: Jumalauta's Game Boy demo that placed 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Stream 2009: a sequence of big slogan screens such as "Opinions lead to conflict" and "We crack your mind".
why: A concept piece with a political edge, tagged for glitch and noise aesthetics, and a podium finish at Stream 2009.

summary: Masters of Electric City's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by bob_er with music by Dhor, which came second in the demo compo at Glucholazy 2008.
why: A podium finish at Glucholazy 2008, and tagged as a text-mode production, so worth a look for what the Atari's character modes can be pushed to do.

summary: Serato's 256-byte Commodore 64 intro, a raycast grayscale city flight that won the 256 Byte Intro Oldschool compo at Lovebyte 2025.
why: Sceners call it an impressive port for fitting into a single block. Once its precalculation finishes, it runs as fast as the screenshot suggests, and some already treat it as the new visual reference for 256 bytes.

quote.text: This might just be the new reference for 256b (for visuals, LFT still rules what comes to aural pleasure).

summary: Black Sun's finished C64 demo, a bug-fixed 100% version of their earlier party release with additions and a note. Code by Nitro, Snerg and Ninja, music by Jammer. It placed 5th in Twoje Stare Demo at Decrunch 2015.
why: Sceners single out the shaded, moving-light animation on the android's face, the plot effects and vectors, and Jammer's otherworldly soundtrack. Several call it fresh and well coded for only the group's second demo.

quote.text: I love that mask with the moving light source. And the soundtrack is plain and simply insane!

summary: Dual Crew Shining's Game Boy Color demo, placed 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2012. Code by Dox and Peitchi, graphics by Vodka and thUg, music by Wiklund.
why: A Game Boy Color entry that held its own in a mixed oldskool compo at Revision, and it runs as an endless loop once the parts are done.

summary: Impact's Amstrad CPC demo from 2021, with code by Demoniak, graphics by Kris, design by CMP and music by Mast. It is built around filled 3D objects.
why: A recent CPC 3D showcase from Impact with no compo entry on record. It was well received on Pouët.

summary: A short C64 one-file demo by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded with music by Virgill and graphics by CONS, that placed third in the oldschool realtime demo compo at Nordlicht 2013.
why: Sceners call it stylish and well made, picking out the floating cubes, the treated face picture and Virgill's music. The usual complaint is that it ends too soon.
highlights: CONS face picture with reddish blur

quote.text: Stylish - the logo infade - the cubes with one side red/blue and the CONS pic with the reddish blur - the noise at the end... really really well made!

summary: A C64 promo for Generation 64, a Swedish book about the Commodore 64 scene, with code by Shadow, graphics by Mermaid, music by Danko and text by Spelpappan. It won the Other Demo compo at Gerp 2014.
why: Sceners liked it as a neat presentation, singling out the portrait of author Spelpappan. Mermaid points out that it only looks PETSCII-like and isn't built from PETSCII characters.

quote.text: this is a nice presentation anyway.

summary: A 256-byte ZX Spectrum intro by Kael and Fyrex of Mayhem, which won the LowEnd 256b Intro compo at DiHalt 2018.
why: It took first place in the LowEnd 256-byte intro competition at DiHalt 2018, so it's a good example of how much fits into a tiny Spectrum program.

summary: Censor Design's two-disk-side C64 demo with a Las Vegas theme, winner of the C64 demo compo at Mysdata 2026. A big crew of coders, musicians and graphicians deliver a fast run of effect and picture screens.
why: Sceners single out the second disk side's effects, Talent's unusual pixel technique and screens that move and rotate freely, ignoring the 8x8 grid and colour limits. Several call the music superb.

quote.text: The 8x8 grid simply does not exist for you - the whole screen is a free canvas where things can move and rotate freely  with no colour limitations.

summary: A Halloween-themed four-disk-side Commodore 64 co-op demo by Pretzel Logic, Offence, Bonzai, Atlantis, Genesis Project, Wrath Designs and Lethargy, released as The Pumpkins. It won the demo compo at Zoo 2022.
why: Sceners praise its consistent spooky theme, polished presentation and a soundtrack by many composers that still hangs together. They single out the VHS rewind and old-movie effects, the turn-disk parts and the little intermissions.

quote.text: so many themes by so many composers and it feels like one piece, never insistent, always engaging.

summary: Placebo's ZX Spectrum demo, second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2001, with code and music by Sairoos, graphics by Paracels and objects by D-Man.
why: It took second place in the Spectrum demo competition at Chaos Constructions 2001 and is well regarded on Pouët.

summary: Onslaught's C64 demo that placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010: Zak McKracken's bedroom from the classic adventure, redrawn with richer graphics, with Zak walking around and talking. Code by Enthusi, graphics by Veto, music by ReD.
why: Sceners praised it as a cool, original idea with a style unlike the usual demo, and singled out the upgraded graphics of a much-loved game. Several hoped it was a preview of a full remake.

quote.text: This is a totally cool and original demo. The style is drastically different from the norm.

summary: lft's C64 demo from Datastorm 2013, where it placed 7th in the C64 demo compo: a VSP-scrolled logo with a long scroller explaining the cause of the infamous VSP crash and how to avoid it in code.
why: A technical article in demo form. Sceners credit it with finally explaining the VSP crash as a DRAM metastability problem and showing crash-free VSP scrolling that works on crash-prone machines.
highlights: code, graphics and music by lft

quote.text: This is so damm cool, you solved a c64 mystery.. a straight 10 from me... congratulations!!

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Arkos and Benediction, with code by Krusty, graphics by Voxfreax and music by Targhan. It placed 4th in the Oldskool 4k Intro compo at Revision 2017.
why: A size-limited CPC intro that held its own in a competitive oldskool compo at Revision, and its source is available for anyone curious how it fits in 4K.

summary: Fairlight's two-disk-side C64 story demo that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2025, following three characters on a road trip, with code by Trident, graphics by Soya and music by Fegolhuzz.
why: Sceners praise how it weaves a funny, heartfelt story together with C64 effects in a coherent flow. Many say it made them laugh out loud, and they single out the parallax greetings, bobs and sideborder tricks.

quote.text: You (again!) managed to weave together a captivating story and C64 demo effects into a coherent flow. Wonderful work.

summary: Ultimate Megademo is a 1992 Amstrad CPC megademo by Face Hugger, who handled the code, graphics and music on his own.
why: A one-person megademo from the early CPC scene, with every part coded, drawn and scored by Face Hugger. It's well liked on Pouët.
highlights: shaded ball objects over a reflective floor

summary: A 32-byte Atari 8-bit intro by JAC! that fills the screen with simulated TV noise. The video title presents it as a collection of noise routines in 32 and 16 bytes.
why: A small study in how much static a few bytes of code can throw up on an Atari, with blue, patterned and grey noise variations. It runs without sound.

summary: Genesis Project's Commodore PET demo, coded by Elder0010 with graphics by Elder0010 and LRNZ, placing third in the Wild compo at Gubbdata 2022.
why: A recent demo for the PET, a machine with only a character display to work with, and it placed in the Wild competition at Gubbdata 2022.

summary: Black Sun's C64 demo, released as a 90% version, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Breakpoint 2010. Code by Nitro, Snerg and Ninja, with graphics and music by Jammer plus guest artists.
why: Sceners single out the light-shaded face, the vector parts built from bobs and multiplexed sprites, and Jammer's soundtrack, which many rank among his best. It was seen as a big step forward for the group.

quote.text: Some really nice effects (face, multiplexed 3D sprites), an excellent soundtrack and a visual style that just speaks to my cyberpunk heart.

summary: Nuance's Vectrex demo, placed 2nd in the Low End Demo compo at The Ultimate Meeting 2013. Code by Nitro, graphics by Bitbreaker and Widdy, music by FieserWolf.
why: A rare demo for the Vectrex's vector display from a team better known on the C64, and a runner-up at The Ultimate Meeting 2013.

summary: The Noisy Bunch's C64 demo, placed 7th in the demo compo at X 2012: a SID-focused follow-up to Vicious Sid with a long list of coders, musicians and artists including Jeroen Tel, 4-Mat and Mahoney.
why: Sceners treat it as a showcase of new SID techniques, singling out polyphonic chords on a single SID channel, a 15 kHz sample part, a reverb part and Protracker modules played on the C64.

quote.text: Polyphonic chords on a single Sid channel?? That alone is worth a perfect ten. And The 15KHz sample part... I stared at it for a good few minutes.
